messages:
Raj: FYI just finished canary for client v1.8 (10% traffic). I'm seeing a small spike of streaming handshake failures on paged endpoints — started ~3m after rollout.

oncall-bot: Incident opened: INC-2026-1976543210  Streaming handshake errors observed during client v1.8 canary

Kate: logs show a lot of `ERR_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` and `frame mismatch` coming from the proxy for /v1/generate/paged.

Lin: confirmed on backend: paged handler returns 200 + chunked body, but the client side aborts at websocket upgrade with `frame mismatch`. Looks like frame-level handshake change.

Evan: I'm going to stop the canary and roll back. Immediate action = kill canary routing. running: 
```
redwood rollout kill --deployment client-1.8 --canary
```

deploy-bot: Kill-switch applied to client-1.8 canary; new canary traffic set to 0%. Current canary sessions will continue until they reconnect.

Raj: good call. CS is watching, we need a quick customer impact summary.

cs-ops: We already have pings from 3 dedicated customers (Atlassia, Formsly, PayGrid). They're reporting streaming errors. Can we give ETA?

Kate: fastest mitigation is full rollback to 1.7. Alternative is a gateway shim but that takes longer. Recommend rollback.

Evan: initiating rollback to client 1.7 now: 
```
redwood deploy rollback --service client --to-version 1.7 --force
```

Lin: metrics: 5xx on paging climbed to ~8% during the canary window, dropping after the kill-switch but there are still live sessions from the canary that fail intermittently. We may need to purge those sessions.

Raj: action list:
- Evan: finish rollback and confirm request success rates normal
- Lin: plan and run session purge for gateways with high failure rates
- Kate: create incident page + customer impact table
- cs-ops: send initial customer comms blurb

Evan: rollback started, ETA ~4m. I'll post completion.

oncall-bot: Deploy event: rollback(client:1.8 -> 1.7) started by Evan at 1976543272

Evan: rollback finished. Routing reverted to baseline. Prometheus: paging 5xx for /v1/generate/paged dropped from 8% -> 0.4% within ~3 minutes.

Kate: confirmed with dashboards. New sessions healthy. Sessions opened during the canary window still show failures. Lin, can we safely purge those sessions?

Lin: yes. We'll target gateways with >10% session fail rate. Example purge command: 
```
scripts/purge_sessions.sh --gateway g-nyc-3 --filter 'started>1976543200' --dry-run
```
Then execute without --dry-run if looks good.

Lin: executed purge on g-nyc-3 and g-eu-1 (affected zones). Reconnect rate ~92% within 60s, errors for older sessions falling quickly.

cs-ops: sending customers: "We detected a canary release of client v1.8 that introduced a frame-level change causing handshake failures for a subset of paged streaming sessions. We halted the rollout and rolled back to v1.7. New sessions are healthy; weare purging impacted sessions to allow reconnects. No data loss is expected." (sending now to Atlassia, Formsly, PayGrid) 

Raj: severity: S2 (partial outage for small number of customers). Preliminary root cause: client v1.8 introduced a frame/handshake format change and our gateway didn't accept it. Compatibility tests missed this.

Evan: creating RCA ticket and postmortem. Actions: add compatibility matrix tests between client frame versions and gateway, and gate frame-format bumps with a feature-flag check so canaries can't roll out frame changes without flag enabled.

Kate: followups: make automated alert to rollback if paging 5xx > 2% for >2m during canary, and draft a CS checklist (blurb + timeline + what to expect).

Lin: handing off to night on-call: @Maya — brief: rollback complete, purge done for affected gateways, customers notified, RCA in progress. If you see any new spike escalate to Eng Lead. Links below.

Maya: ack. Please drop links to runbook + incident page. I'll monitor every 10m.

Lin: incident page: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-1976543210
Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-handshake
Rollback log: https://deploys.redwood/internal/logs/rollback-1976543272

Maya: taking over monitoring. I'll post if anything unusual shows up.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-1976543210 moved to monitoring. Owner: Maya. Last update by Lin.
